stem: Five students P, Q, R, S, T are seated in a row. T is at the leftmost seat. Q is seated immediately to the right of P. R is not adjacent to S. S is seated to the left of Q. Who is seated second from the right?

per_option_rationale.rationale: T at pos 1 (leftmost). S left of Q, Q right of P: this forces the chain ...S...P,Q... With T at pos 1 and S somewhere left of Q, the valid order is T,S,P,Q,R placing Q at position 4 (second from right).

Ignoring that R must not be adjacent to S, one possible order could be T,P,Q,S,R. Here P is second from left not second from right; picking P at second from right ignores the non-adjacency constraint.
Placing R immediately right of S (reversing the non-adjacency tie-breaker to adjacency) forces a different arrangement where R occupies the second-from-right position.
Reading 'second from the right' as 'second from the left' gives S (who is at position 2 in the correct arrangement T,S,P,Q,R).

explanation: T anchors position 1 (leftmost). S must be left of Q, and Q must be immediately right of P. The chain S,P,Q must fit in positions 2-4 or later. Placing S,P,Q at positions 2,3,4 leaves R at position 5. Check: R(5) and S(2) are not adjacent (|5-2|=3). Valid unique arrangement: T,S,P,Q,R. Second from right = position 4 = Q.

explanation_sections.punchline: The non-adjacency clue (R not next to S) is the tie-breaker that fixes R at the far right, not Q.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: T at pos 1. S left of Q and Q right of P gives the block ...S...P,Q. Only placement fitting T at left is T,S,P,Q,? with R at pos 5. Verify R-S non-adjacency: |5-2|=3 passes. Second from right (pos 4) = Q.
explanation_sections.lesson: Negative clues (not adjacent) serve as tie-breakers; test them last after the positive chain is placed.
explanation_sections.timing: About 80-90 seconds. The trap is misreading second from right as second from left, giving S.
